new_statements.rule_in_words: Sadu is treated as a lexical-tone language with no word stress reported; the DoReCo transcriptions (Xu & Bai) mark every syllable with one of five Chao-numbered tones (55, 42, 33, 21, 313) and carry no stress marks. No source seen states a stress position.
new_statements.domain_note: Typological survey table coding 'word prosody type' per sample language; the classification for Sadu is sourced to the DoReCo corpus itself rather than to the printed grammar (Bai & Xu 2012), so it is second-hand and coarse (tone vs stress vs phrase language).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same variety: Sadu 撒都 (autonym sa55 du42 pho313), spoken in Jiaoyuan 椒园, Xincun 新村 and Dashuitang 大水塘 hamlets, Hongta District, Yuxi, Yunnan; speakers officially registered as Bai nationality but the language is Loloish (Glottolog sadu1234, no ISO code). DoReCo texts come mainly from Jiaoyuan speakers (surname Li). Not to be confused with 'Sadu Koireng' (Kuki-Chin, Manipur; Waikhom 2013), which the earlier access cache had mismatched to this key.

sources.note: A 民族语文 '概况' sketch (8 pp.) based on the authors' 2009- fieldwork; the genre's fixed layout is 语音 (声母, 韵母, 声调 inventories with examples, 音节/音变) - 词汇 - 语法, so this is the first-hand journal statement of the Sadu tone inventory, three months before the 396-page grammar. The abstract read (NCPSSD) gives location, population, Bai classification and Loloish affiliation ('既不同于大理白语，也不同于周边彝语南部方言尼苏话、纳苏话、山苏话') but no tone figures; the same authors' DoReCo transcriptions (a work listed here) use five tone values 55, 33, 21, 42, 313, which is what the 声调 paragraph should list.
